claims.text: Computerised cognitive behavioural therapy (cCBT) provides clinical benefit for depression in adolescents and young adults.
Computerised cognitive behavioural therapy (cCBT) provides clinical benefit for anxiety in adolescents and young adults.
The benefits of digital health interventions in managing ADHD in children and young people are uncertain.
The benefits of digital health interventions in managing autism in children and young people are uncertain.
The benefits of digital health interventions in managing psychosis in children and young people are uncertain.
The benefits of digital health interventions in managing eating disorders in children and young people are uncertain.
Evidence regarding the cost-effectiveness of digital health interventions for children and young people is lacking.

evidence.description: The meta-review findings provide some support for the clinical benefit of DHIs, particularly cCBT, for depression in adolescents and young adults.
The meta-review findings provide some support for the clinical benefit of DHIs, particularly cCBT, for anxiety in adolescents and young adults.
Systematic review of 30 new RCTs showed that benefits of DHIs in managing ADHD are uncertain.
Systematic review of 30 new RCTs showed that benefits of DHIs in managing autism are uncertain.
Systematic review of 30 new RCTs showed that benefits of DHIs in managing psychosis are uncertain.
Systematic review of 30 new RCTs showed that benefits of DHIs in managing eating disorders are uncertain.
Review findings indicated that evidence is lacking regarding the cost-effectiveness of DHIs.

methodologies.name: Meta-review and updated systematic review
methodologies.description: Meta-review of 21 scoping, narrative, systematic, or meta-analytical reviews combined with an updated systematic review of 30 RCTs of DHIs published in the last 3 years.

limitations.text: Existing clinical trials of DHIs suffer from variable uptake and engagement, small sample sizes, and lack of blinded outcome assessment.
Existing research lacks an agreed typology/taxonomy for DHIs and poorly specifies the level of human support.
Clinical trials of DHIs frequently combine different comparators and rely on short-term follow-up.

future_work.text: Implementation of recommendations addressing key research questions and methodological issues for the evaluation and clinical adoption of DHIs for children and young people.
